blocks.content: Quiz: What does mobile-first CSS mean?
Tap an option below to answer:
Writing CSS only for mobile and ignoring desktop.
Making the desktop layout look like mobile.
Base styles for the smallest screen, add layout for larger viewports with min-width media queries.
Base styles for the smallest screen, add layout for larger viewports with min-width media queries.
Mobile-first absolutely supports desktop. It just reaches desktop through min-width layers rather than starting there. Base styles run on all viewports, only the additions are gated.
max-width is actually the desktop-first approach. You start wide and use max-width to narrow things back down. Mobile-first flips it, start narrow and add complexity upward with min-width.
max-width is actually the desktop-first approach. You start wide and use max-width to narrow things back down. Mobile-first flips it, start narrow and add complexity upward with min-width.
That would just be a bad desktop experience. Mobile-first means you write for mobile first in the cascade, then add more layout as space allows.
Mobile-first means base styles target the smallest viewport and you layer on larger layouts with min-width, not max-width.
Mobile-first means base styles target the smallest viewport and you layer on larger layouts with min-width, not max-width.
